issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
source_clause: Data Stewards are responsible for documented processes including risk assessment, disaster recovery, business continuity, software testing and revision controls; Data Custodians implement change management/revision controls.
operational_implication: Assessment evidence should show named stewardship/custody roles and the actual artifacts used for testing, revision control, continuity, and risk decisions.
discovery_question: For each ESS/RIS/IAM service, who is the Data Steward and Data Custodian, and which current artifacts demonstrate their responsibilities?
applicability_caveat: Published role requirement does not establish that a named team follows it consistently or that every in-scope service has the same control design.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
source_clause: Critical business processes should be performed by separate individuals; developer, system administrator, and database administrator responsibilities should not overlap unless authorized by the Data Steward.
operational_implication: Interview and artifact review should distinguish normal role separation, authorized overlap, and emergency/low-capacity exceptions.
discovery_question: Where do development, administration, database, release, and approval duties overlap, and what stewardship approval/evidence exists for necessary overlap?
applicability_caveat: The policy does not prove the current team topology or mean all overlap is prohibited; authorized exceptions and actual service risk must be established.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
source_clause: Physical and electronic access is controlled based on classification and risk, with processes for timely removal of access.
operational_implication: Assessment should trace joiner-mover-leaver events from approval through revocation in the actual systems used by each service.
discovery_question: What events trigger access changes, how quickly do they propagate, and what evidence proves deprovisioning reached repositories, pipelines, databases, consoles, and support tools?
applicability_caveat: Policy intent is not evidence of actual revocation latency or control coverage.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
policy_or_section: IT-18 > Change Management > System and Application Software
source_clause: System and application software must be tested before production installation, protected from unauthorized changes, and updated commensurate with vulnerability risk.
operational_implication: Release assessment should recover what was tested, which revision was approved, and whether the tested revision is the deployed revision.
discovery_question: For recent normal and urgent changes, what evidence links source/config revision, test results, approval, built artifact, and production deployment?
applicability_caveat: The policy defines required practice but not test depth, automation level, release cadence, or whether a particular historical release complied.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
source_clause: Systems handling non-public institutional data require change-control management covering change requests, approvals, testing, and final implementation; scope includes physical hardware and cloud services.
operational_implication: For non-public data systems, a sampled change should be traceable across request, authorization, verification, and implementation records.
discovery_question: Which in-scope services handle non-public data, what is the authoritative change record for each, and how are cloud/configuration changes included?
applicability_caveat: Applicability depends on system data classification; a workflow ticket alone does not demonstrate effective control.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Security Policy
policy_or_section: IT-18 > Preventive Measures, Backup and Recovery
source_clause: Institutional data must be sufficiently backed up and recoverable; computerized systems critical to the University must have written and tested disaster-recovery plans.
operational_implication: Operational assessment should connect stated criticality to tested recovery evidence, ownership, dependencies, and recovery priorities.
discovery_question: Which ESS/RIS/IAM services are designated critical, when was recovery last exercised, what dependencies were included, and what result/evidence was retained?
applicability_caveat: A written plan or backup configuration is not proof that recovery objectives are achievable; criticality and test results require engagement evidence.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Institutional Data Policy
source_clause: Institutional data has four sensitivity levels: Critical, Restricted, University-Internal, and Public; unless otherwise classified it is University-Internal.
operational_implication: Data-handling review should request the authoritative classification used by each application, dataset, log, export, and integration rather than infer sensitivity from content labels.
discovery_question: What classification has the responsible Data Trustee assigned to each sampled dataset and system, and where is that decision recorded?
applicability_caveat: The default does not authorize the assessment team to reclassify data; only the accountable University role can establish classification.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Institutional Data Policy
source_clause: Institutional Data that is moved, copied, extended, or propagated remains Institutional Data and applicable policies continue to apply.
operational_implication: Copies used in test environments, troubleshooting exports, analytics extracts, CI artifacts, backups, and support attachments should retain handling requirements.
discovery_question: Where is production-derived data copied for development, test, support, analytics, logs, or backups, and how is classification/handling preserved across those copies?
applicability_caveat: This statement does not prove that every technical artifact contains institutional data; determine actual content and authorized use first.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Institutional Data Policy
source_clause: Restricted/Critical access is approved by the Data Steward; use of authorized non-public data is limited to the purpose for which access was granted; protections apply to copies.
operational_implication: Access review should bind entitlement to business purpose and steward authorization, including copied/derived working data.
discovery_question: For sampled privileged or non-public-data access, what purpose, approving Steward, expiry/review basis, and downstream copies can be traced?
applicability_caveat: Authorization evidence does not by itself establish least privilege or technical enforcement; both need direct evidence.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Institutional Data Policy
source_clause: Public or University-Internal data may be repurposed when authorized by the Data Trustee; secondary use/repurposing of Restricted or Critical data is strictly prohibited.
operational_implication: Any proposed reuse of operational, support, development, or analytics data for new tooling—including AI-enabled workflows—needs classification and purpose review before assumptions about permissible reuse.
discovery_question: Do any developer/support/AI workflows reuse institutional data for a purpose different from the original access grant, and what classification/authorization governs that use?
applicability_caveat: This row does not assert that ESS, RIS, or IAM currently uses AI or repurposes data; it defines a discovery boundary only.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Enterprise Authentication Authorization and Access Policy
policy_or_section: IT-15 > Campus Software Acquisitions and Development
source_clause: Locally developed software should implement Enterprise Authentication whenever possible; third-party software/services should support secure authentication, current enterprise authentication interoperability, and standard login IDs; exceptions require ISPO review.
operational_implication: Application assessment should distinguish enterprise-auth-integrated services from local authentication and recover the approved rationale/review for exceptions.
discovery_question: Which in-scope applications use enterprise authentication, which rely on local/vendor authentication, and what current review/transition plan exists for exceptions?
applicability_caveat: The policy does not imply every application can use the same mechanism; technical feasibility and approved exceptions must be confirmed.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: Enterprise Authentication Authorization and Access Policy
source_clause: For non-public data, Data Stewards establish account/service eligibility, creation, maintenance, retention, and expiration; Data Custodians periodically review privileges and modify/remove/deactivate accounts as roles change.
operational_implication: IAM evidence should cover eligibility rules, periodic review, role-change handling, account/service expiration, and proof of completed changes.
discovery_question: For people and service identities, who defines review periods and eligibility, how are role changes detected, and what sampled evidence shows privileges were actually changed?
applicability_caveat: Policy establishes responsibility, not review frequency for every service or evidence that reviews are currently effective.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: IT Accessibility Policy
source_clause: IT-26 applies to electronic/information technology used by the University, including third-party materials used for official functions; responsible individuals are to include accessibility in all phases of the software lifecycle.
operational_implication: Accessibility evidence should appear during requirements, design, build/test, procurement/integration, release, and maintenance—not only after a complaint.
discovery_question: For sampled internally developed and third-party applications, where do accessibility requirements, test results, defects, exceptions, and remediation ownership appear across the lifecycle?
applicability_caveat: Policy coverage does not establish conformance of a particular application; measured accessibility requires product-specific evidence.

issuer: University of Iowa Information Security and Policy Office
title: IT Accessibility Policy
source_clause: The University maintains accessibility evaluation in procurement; exceptions require documented approval when criteria such as undue burden, fundamental alteration, or unavailable accessible version apply.
operational_implication: Assessment should recover accessibility evaluation and exception records for material third-party technology dependencies in scope.
discovery_question: For recently acquired or renewed technology used by ESS/RIS/IAM, what accessibility evaluation was performed and how are approved exceptions/remediation tracked?
applicability_caveat: The assessment is not a procurement audit and should not infer a defect solely from the existence of an exception.

title: Standards for Accessible Technology
source_clause: WCAG 2.1 Level AA is the University technical standard for web pages, sites, and applications delivered using web protocols; separate Section 508/WCAG 2.0 AA references apply to non-web technologies.
operational_implication: Web application review can use WCAG 2.1 AA as the University-stated technical baseline and should retain product-specific test evidence.
discovery_question: Which in-scope user interfaces are web vs non-web, what standard is applied to each, and what current test evidence/known exceptions exist?
applicability_caveat: A named standard is not evidence of conformance; do not convert this into an unsupported maturity or compliance score.

title: Records Management
policy_or_section: Chapter 17.3 > Definition and Identification of Records
source_clause: University records include electronic records, databases, communications, and other data compilations made/received in official University business.
operational_implication: Engineering and operational artifacts can be records depending on their function; the responsible University records owner should classify them rather than the assessment assuming all logs/tickets/repos have the same status.
discovery_question: Which release, approval, incident, access, support, and decision artifacts are official records for each service, and who owns that determination?
applicability_caveat: Record status is functional/contextual; not every draft, duplicate, log, backup, or engineering artifact is automatically an official record.

title: Records Management
source_clause: Official records are subject to retention requirements; transitory/convenience records include duplicate copies, backups, drafts, and miscellaneous correspondence without official significance.
operational_implication: Assessment should separate authoritative decision/evidence records from disposable working copies and understand how systems of record are designated.
discovery_question: Which artifact is the official record for approvals, releases, access reviews, incidents, and accepted requirements, and which repository/ticket/log copies are transitory?
applicability_caveat: The examples are categories, not an automatic classification rule for every technical system; record owners must resolve ambiguous cases.

title: Records Management
source_clause: Official records use the Records Management Program/Retention Schedule; University minimum categories are five years, ten years, or permanent by record type, and audits/litigation/public-record requests/legal holds can suspend disposal.
operational_implication: Retention configuration for assessment-relevant evidence should be tied to record type and hold requirements, not a universal engineering-log period.
discovery_question: For the records used to evidence release, security, access, incidents, and approvals, what retention schedule applies and how are legal/audit/public-record holds propagated to the storage systems?
applicability_caveat: Do not assign a retention period from this summary alone; the exact record type and current schedule entry must be confirmed.

title: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resources
source_clause: Backup/recovery systems must follow University disaster-recovery guidance; institutional systems use security controls under University policies/procedures; operations may require backups, activity logging, and monitoring.
operational_implication: Operational evidence review should distinguish necessary service telemetry/backup from assumptions of continuous employee monitoring and should account for public-record/discovery obligations.
discovery_question: What logs/backups are necessary for service operation, security, recovery, and records obligations; who can access them; and what retention/access controls apply?
applicability_caveat: The policy acknowledges operational logging/monitoring but does not prescribe a single observability stack or prove coverage/effectiveness for any service.
